reading.body:
Robert Latta's AI record is 13 dated events: seven committee contributions from AI companies, four recorded votes, and two bills. The money is the densest signal, and it runs from Google, Amazon, Microsoft, Meta, and Qualcomm.

The contributions total $13,500 across seven filings between June 2025 and June 2026. Google gave twice, in June 2025. Amazon gave twice, in September 2025 and June 2026. Microsoft, Meta, and Qualcomm each gave once. The giving is steady rather than clustered, which is what a member on a relevant committee would expect to see.

The legislative record is thinner than the money. Latta sponsored one bill, the Collaboration on Adversarial Threats and Security Risks Act, in July 2026, and cosponsored the AI OVERWATCH Act in December 2025. Both entries carry the bill's latest status date rather than an introduction date, so the timeline of his involvement is not recoverable from this data. The four votes are all yea, all on suspension, and the underlying bills are identified only by number.

What this does not show is causation, and the data says so directly. Contributions and votes are placed in date order for reading, not to claim one produced the other. It also does not show committee assignments, which is the mechanism that would make either the money or the bills matter. Nothing here connects to compute, buildings, or power. This is a money and voting record, and it stops there.

summary: Every dated AI event this site holds for Robert Latta: bills sponsored or cosponsored, recorded votes on AI bills, and money from AI company and AI-focused political committees, newest first. 13 events.
